title: Comments & Clean Code 🧹
description: Leave helpful notes and adopt good coding habits from day one.

slides.title: Why Comment? 💬
slides.content:
# Comments Explain the 'Why'

HTML comments look like this:
```html
<!-- This is a comment -->
```
- They are completely ignored by the browser.
- Use them to leave notes for yourself or other developers.
- Explain complex sections or mark reminders ("TODO: add image here").
- But avoid stating the obvious – code should be as self‑documenting as possible.

quizData.question: What is the correct syntax for an HTML comment?
quizData.explanation: HTML comments are written between <!-- and --> markers.

slides.title: Indentation & Formatting 📏
slides.content:
# Make Your Code Readable

- Always indent nested elements (use 2 or 4 spaces, never mix with tabs).
- Put opening and closing tags on separate lines when the content is long.
- Use lowercase for tag names (HTML5 is case‑insensitive, but lowercase is the convention).

Clean code is faster to debug and looks professional.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## VS Code Shortcut

In VS Code, you can format your entire document instantly with `Shift + Alt + F`. Use it often to keep your HTML neat and readable.

quizData.question: Comments are visible to visitors when they view the page source.
quizData.explanation: Yes, HTML comments appear in the page source (View > Source). Never put sensitive information in them!
